title: Postern status response
description: Response body of GET /postern/v0/status. Answerable at conformance Level 1 and without credentials. See SPEC.md section 4.4.

agent.description: Which agent this runner serves. SPEC.md section 1.5 says the identifier appears here as well as in describe, and section 2.2's identity rule - one runner, one agent, its port that agent's address - is only checkable when it does. Only id is required: section 4.4's example carries version beside it and nothing obliges it.

id.description: Agent identifier (SPEC.md section 1.5). The same string describe reports and the distributor paths address.

entitlement.description: SPEC.md section 5.1 requires a runner with no distributor to report state as not_required, so the block is not omissible: saying nothing is indistinguishable from a runner that has not implemented entitlement at all, which is the one thing a client reads this to find out.

state.description: not_required means no distributor is configured; the runner MUST NOT refuse to run on entitlement grounds. unknown means the runner cannot presently vouch: inside a declared grace period, or never having obtained an answer (SPEC.md section 5.7). checked_at tells those two apart.

checked_at.description: The distributor's own read time, propagated unchanged from the entitlement check. A runner MUST NOT re-stamp it with its own clock. REQUIRED when state is active or revoked. A 404 carries no such value, and there the runner reports its own receipt time instead (SPEC.md section 5.7.4).

stale_after_seconds.description: REQUIRED when state is active or revoked. With grace_seconds it bounds how long a revoked entitlement can keep working; under revoked it is instead when the runner re-checks. After a 404 the runner supplies its own re-check cadence, reusing the distributor's last value where it has one (SPEC.md section 5.7.4).

grace_seconds.description: The grace the distributor declared for an unreachable check (SPEC.md sections 5.3, 5.7), where the runner has been told one. A client needs it beside checked_at to say when an agent running through an outage stops.

update.description: What the runner learned when it asked its distributor whether a newer version of the agent exists (SPEC.md section 4.4). OPTIONAL, and present only where such a check actually ran — a runner with no version check configured omits it, which is a different fact from a check that ran and found no distributor to ask. How a runner obtains the answer is the distributor's to define; this specification adds no path for it.

state.description: not_required: no distributor is configured, mirroring entitlement's own state (section 5.1). unreachable: one is and could not be asked — a client reads this as not known, never as out of date, and a runner MUST NOT refuse to start or to run because of it (section 4.4). current / update_available: the check succeeded, and the running version and the reported one are equal or are not.

current.description: The runner's own describe.agent.version. Present whenever it is knowable, unreachable included: a runner always knows what it is running, whatever it could not reach.

latest.description: The version the distributor reported. Present only under current and update_available, those being the only states in which one was obtained.

limits.description: Bounds the runner puts on a run in flight (SPEC.md section 4.5). These belong to the deployment rather than to the agent, which is why they sit here and not in describe: two runners serving one agent may answer differently.

max_run_seconds.description: The longest a run may take before the runner stops it with 504 run_timeout. REQUIRED where the runner imposes a limit at all, absent where it does not. A runner MUST NOT declare a bound longer than the shortest one it can actually enforce.

max_output_bytes.description: The largest artifact the runner will return from a bytes output, measured before base64 rather than after. REQUIRED where the runner bounds one at all, absent where it does not (SPEC.md section 4.1.4).

idempotency_retention_seconds.description: How long the runner replays an Idempotency-Key it has already answered (SPEC.md section 4.2). SHOULD be declared by a runner that honours the header and can state a window; a client MUST NOT assume any particular one where none is declared, and a retry arriving after the window has lapsed is answered by a fresh execution rather than refused. This bounds a promise rather than a run, which is what makes it the odd member here.

max_concurrent_runs.description: How many runs the runner will have in flight at once; beyond it, run and stream answer 503 unavailable. At least 1 — a runner that will run nothing says so with its level and a 501, which tells a client retrying is pointless, where a 0 here reads as a temporary condition.
